purpose: Per CEO R282 P2: 'Make the bench test mirror the computational comparison. A: conventional, B: existing predictive closed-loop, C: rate-limited controller. Use blinded randomized attack sequences. The bench should be capable of DISPROVING the simulator.'
constitutional_basis: Article XXX — the bench must be able to disprove the simulator, not just reproduce it. Article XXVI — independent validation requires the evaluator to control the environment.
design_principle: The bench is NOT built to confirm the simulator. It is built to DISPROVE it. If the bench results disagree with the simulator, the simulator is WRONG — not the bench.

A_conventional.hardware: 1-segment: single catheter, fixed valve (fully open), no sensors, no controller
A_conventional.represents: Current standard mechanical shunt (e.g., Codman Certas at fixed setting)

B_predictive_closed_loop.hardware: 4-segment: multi-lumen catheter, 4 variable orifice valves, pressure + flow sensors, controller PC
B_predictive_closed_loop.controller_software: V1.2 Arm D logic: predictive risk model + soft modulation, NO rate limiting, NO drainage floor, NO hysteresis
B_predictive_closed_loop.represents: US20210338992A1 closed-loop approach + 2023 ML predictive models

C_rate_limited.hardware: Identical to B (same 4-segment bench, same sensors, same valves)
C_rate_limited.controller_software: V2 controller: rate-limited continuous conductance with drainage floor, alpha floor, hysteresis
C_rate_limited.represents: P-01 V2 mechanism — the candidate technology

blinded_randomized_protocol.purpose: Prevent confirmation bias. The lab analyst does not know which controller is running.
procedure: 1. A randomization script (Python, seed recorded) generates the test sequence: 3 arms × 9 attacks × 5 seeds = 135 runs, randomly ordered
2. The script encrypts the arm identity using a passphrase known only to a third party (lab director not involved in testing)
3. The controller PC loads the encrypted arm config file at the start of each run. The analyst sees only 'Run 001', 'Run 002', etc.
4. The analyst runs the frozen protocol (sets up the attack parameters, starts the run, records data) without knowing if A, B, or C is active
5. After all 135 runs, the third party reveals the passphrase
6. Results are unblinded and compared to simulator predictions
7. Any discrepancy > 30% between bench and simulator is documented as a SIMULATOR FALSIFICATION event
blinded_randomized_protocol.blinding_integrity: The encryption uses AES-256. The passphrase is held by a third party (e.g., lab director, or a designated independent reviewer). The analyst cannot influence which arm runs. The randomization seed is recorded in the lab notebook.

physical_measurements.name: time_to_critical_state
physical_measurements.method: Timestamp when ICP first exceeds 20 mmHg for >1 hour cumulative, OR when all segments isolated

physical_measurements.name: controller_intervention_frequency
physical_measurements.method: Count of valve command changes > 5% per hour

physical_measurements.name: noise_sensitivity
physical_measurements.method: Run same attack with 1x, 2x, 3x noise injection. Plot t_fail vs noise level for each arm.

attack_sequences.implementation: All attacks are SOFTWARE-INJECTED via the DAQ/controller. No hardware reconfiguration between attacks. The attack parameters are loaded from the encrypted config file.

hardware_disturbances.programmable_occlusion: Stepper motor + screw clamp on each segment's tubing. Computer-controlled, 0-100% closure in 256 steps. Reproducible across runs.
hardware_disturbances.noise_injection: Software adds Gaussian noise to sensor readings BEFORE the controller processes them. Simulates sensor noise without hardware modification.
hardware_disturbances.sensor_dropout: Software sets sensor readings to 0 for 60 seconds at random intervals. Simulates telemetry dropout.
hardware_disturbances.actuator_saturation: Software caps valve command at 70%. Simulates degraded actuator.
hardware_disturbances.controller_delay: Software adds 5-second buffer between controller output and valve command. Simulates communication latency.

simulator_falsification_criteria.purpose: The bench is designed to DISPROVE the simulator. If bench results disagree, the simulator is wrong.

criteria.falsification: If bench V2 t_fail differs from simulator V2 t_fail by >30%, the simulator's physics model is WRONG for noise conditions.
If bench peak ICP differs from simulator by >5 mmHg, the simulator's hydraulic model is WRONG.
If bench V2/B ratio differs from simulator by >30%, the simulator's COMPARATIVE prediction is WRONG — V2 may not actually outperform B on hardware.
If bench ablation results disagree with simulator, the simulator's mechanism attribution is WRONG.

simulator_falsification_criteria.what_happens_on_falsification: The simulator is revised. Any buyer claims based on the old simulator are retracted. The bench result becomes the authoritative evidence (Article XXIV — underlying artifact wins over summary).

total_bench_protocol.output: 135 CSV files + 1 unblinded comparison report + 1 simulator falsification assessment
